name: Ukraine
summary: Now in its fifth year of full-scale war, Ukraine experienced its deadliest civilian year since 2022 in 2025 — with a 31% increase in casualties driven by intensified drone attacks. 10.8 million people need humanitarian assistance, and over 9.3 million Ukrainians remain displaced inside the country or as refugees abroad.
context:
Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022 triggered Europe's largest displacement crisis since World War II and has caused massive civilian suffering. After nearly four years of war, 2025 proved to be the deadliest for civilians since the initial invasion, with a 31% increase in casualties over 2024. Drone attacks surged 120%, targeting residential areas and energy infrastructure far from the front lines.

Repeated strikes on Ukraine's energy grid created a 'crisis within a crisis' during the 2024–2025 winter. Power blackouts lasting 12–18 hours per day became routine in many regions, forcing millions to survive without heat, light, or running water at temperatures well below freezing. The healthcare system has been a deliberate target, with hundreds of hospitals and medical facilities damaged or destroyed.

The human toll is staggering: at least 15,172 civilians confirmed killed and 41,378 injured since February 2022, with the actual figures likely significantly higher due to access constraints. Over 2.5 million homes have been damaged or destroyed, and 8 million people have been pushed into poverty. Direct damages are estimated at over $176 billion.

About 3.7 million Ukrainians are internally displaced, while 5.6 million are registered as refugees abroad — primarily in Poland, Germany, and other EU countries. Despite high media coverage relative to other crises, the 2026 humanitarian appeal of $2.3 billion remains underfunded.

Ukraine's cultural and infrastructure destruction is also a deliberate strategy: museums, archives, monuments, and historical sites have been targeted, representing an assault not just on people but on Ukrainian identity itself.

donate.name: UNHCR — Ukraine Emergency
donate.description: Providing emergency shelter, legal aid, and protection to displaced Ukrainians both inside the country and as refugees in Europe.

donate.name: ICRC — Ukraine
donate.description: Delivering emergency aid to conflict-affected communities, supporting prisoners of war, and tracing missing persons.

donate.name: World Food Programme — Ukraine
donate.description: Providing food assistance and cash transfers to vulnerable Ukrainians, including the elderly and those near the front lines.

donate.name: WHO — Ukraine
donate.description: Restoring health services, supplying medicines, and coordinating the humanitarian health response across Ukraine.

awareness: Share the reality that 2025 was the deadliest year for Ukrainian civilians since 2022 — escalation is ongoing, not winding down
Highlight the targeting of Ukrainian energy infrastructure and what it means for millions of civilians facing winter without heat or electricity
Amplify documentation of attacks on hospitals, schools, and cultural heritage sites — these are war crimes
Support Ukrainian journalists and media outlets that provide independent, on-the-ground reporting
Counter war fatigue narratives — this crisis has not ended, and sustained attention is critical for political will
political: Urge your representatives to maintain and increase military and humanitarian aid to Ukraine
Support calls to use frozen Russian sovereign assets to fund Ukraine's reconstruction and reparations
Advocate for continued and expanded EU refugee support for the 5.6 million Ukrainians abroad
Push for full accountability at the International Criminal Court for war crimes and crimes against humanity documented in Ukraine
Demand that any peace process include full restoration of Ukrainian sovereignty and accountability for Russian aggression
